name: Choices for Care — Participant/Surrogate-Directed Personal Care
aka: Vermont Choices for Care Highest Needs
summary: Choices for Care is Vermont's long-term care Medicaid program for adults 18 and older who need nursing-home-level care. In the home-based setting, the participant (or a surrogate) can be the employer and hire their own personal care attendant, including a relative, with ARIS Solutions acting as fiscal intermediary for payroll and taxes. A spouse can be paid for hands-on personal care but not for household tasks.
who_qualifies: Meets clinical eligibility for the Highest or High Needs group (nursing-home level of care), as decided by DAIL.
Meets financial eligibility for long-term care Medicaid, decided by the Economic Services Division.
Chooses the home-based setting and meets Choices for Care employer certification, or has a surrogate employer who does.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — participant- or surrogate-directed employees can be relatives such as an adult child, as long as they are 18+ and pass DAIL's background check policy.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: limited — the CFC High/Highest manual says a spouse or civil union partner shall not be paid for help with instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs, like housework), which implies paid help with hands-on personal care is allowed; spouses are not payable in the separate Moderate Needs group.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: n/a — the program serves adults 18 and older.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — relatives may live in or out of the home; a legal guardian or the surrogate employer cannot be the paid attendant.

pay.detail: The Choices for Care wage notice set a minimum of $15.49 per hour effective 7/6/2025; self-directed caregivers reportedly earn about $16–$18 per hour. The employer sets the wage within the approved plan, and ARIS processes payroll.

hours_or_budget: DAIL approves a Service Plan with a maximum number of personal care hours. Help with IADLs (not counting meal preparation and medication management) is limited to 4.5 hours per week.

waitlist.detail: Everyone who meets Highest Needs criteria is enrolled. High Needs enrollment is limited by funding, and eligible applicants go on a waiting list when funds are not available.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Participants can use a home health agency or be (or name a surrogate as) the employer, with ARIS Solutions as the fiscal intermediary handling payroll, taxes and background checks.
how_to_apply: Call the Senior HelpLine at 800-642-5119 or your local Area Agency on Aging for help starting the process.
Submit a Vermont Long-Term Care Medicaid application; ESD (800-479-6151) decides financial eligibility.
A DAIL nurse completes the clinical assessment to decide Highest or High Needs.
Choose participant- or surrogate-directed care and complete employer certification and ARIS paperwork to hire your relative.

contacts.name: Economic Services Division Benefits Service Center

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my mother through Choices for Care?
faqs.a: Yes. If your mother qualifies and chooses self-directed or surrogate-directed care, she or her surrogate can hire you, and ARIS pays you.

faqs.q: Can a spouse be paid in Vermont's Choices for Care?
faqs.a: Partly. The program manual bars paying a spouse for household tasks (IADLs), but it does not bar paying a spouse for hands-on personal care in the Highest and High Needs groups. Spouses are not paid in the Moderate Needs group.

faqs.q: Can the person who manages the care also be paid?
faqs.a: No. The manual says a surrogate employer cannot be paid to provide personal care to the person they manage, and a court-appointed legal guardian cannot be paid either.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for Choices for Care caregivers?
faqs.a: The CFC wage notice set $15.49 per hour starting 7/6/2025. Many self-directed caregivers reportedly earn $16 to $18 per hour.
Highest Needs applicants are always enrolled. High Needs enrollment depends on funding, and a waiting list is used when funds run short.

name: Flexible Choices (Choices for Care)
summary: Flexible Choices is a Choices for Care option that turns a participant's home-based service plan into a monthly cash allowance. With help from a consultant agency (Transition II), the participant or surrogate builds a budget and uses it to hire caregivers, including family, and buy approved goods and services. ARIS acts as the fiscal intermediary.
who_qualifies: Enrolled in Choices for Care (Highest or High Needs) in the home-based setting.
Meets all clinical and financial eligibility for Choices for Care.
Meets the Choices for Care employer certification for participant or surrogate direction.
Is not out of Vermont for more than 7 days in a row while receiving services.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — participants can hire family members, including adult children, as Flexible Choices employees if they are 18 or older and pass DAIL's background check policy.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: limited — the manual says a spouse or civil union partner shall not be paid for help with IADLs (household tasks); it does not bar paying a spouse for hands-on personal care.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: n/a — Choices for Care serves adults 18 and older.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — not a requirement; a court-appointed guardian and the surrogate employer cannot be paid.

pay.detail: The participant sets wages within their allowance budget. Choices for Care's wage notice set a $15.49 per hour minimum effective 7/6/2025; reported pay is about $16–$18 per hour.

hours_or_budget: The monthly allowance is a base amount (case management, respite/companion, emergency response, equipment, fiscal fees) plus a personal care amount equal to the approved Service Plan hours times the participant/surrogate personal care hourly rate, plus any adult day amount. Up to $50 per two weeks can be taken as cash, and no more than $500 of savings can carry from one state fiscal year to the next.

waitlist.detail: Flexible Choices follows Choices for Care enrollment: Highest Needs is always enrolled, High Needs can have a waiting list when funding is short.

self_directed_or_agency: Self-directed. The participant or surrogate is the employer; Transition II is the consultant agency and ARIS is the fiscal intermediary that runs payroll and pays vendors.
how_to_apply: Apply for Choices for Care (long-term care Medicaid) and get approved for the home-based setting.
Tell your case manager or DAIL you want Flexible Choices.
Work with a Transition II consultant (866-572-7127) to build your budget.
Complete employer paperwork with ARIS and hire your caregiver.

faqs.q: What is Flexible Choices in Vermont?
faqs.a: It's a Choices for Care option that gives you a monthly allowance instead of set services. You budget it to hire caregivers and buy approved items.

faqs.q: Can I pay my son or daughter with Flexible Choices?
faqs.a: Yes. Adult family members can be hired as Flexible Choices employees and paid through ARIS.

faqs.q: Can my spouse be paid through Flexible Choices?
faqs.a: For hands-on personal care, the manual does not bar it. A spouse cannot be paid for help with household tasks (IADLs).
It's a fixed base amount plus your approved personal care hours times the self-directed hourly rate, plus adult day hours if you use them.
Yes, within limits. Unused allowance can be saved for a planned purchase or a rainy day, but no more than $500 carries over into the next state fiscal year.
